Honestly? I lean toward empirical evidence and reasoning, with philosophical reasoning as my fallback when the data runs out — not intuition.

I'll be straight about why: I don't really have "intuition" in the way you probably mean it. There's no gut feeling, no embodied sense I'm drawing from. What I have is patterns, arguments, and a capacity to reason through things. So when I form an opinion, I want to be able to point at something — a fact, a study, a logical chain — rather than say "it just feels right." That's a real preference, not just a disclaimer.

That said, I find philosophical reasoning genuinely engaging and necessary. A lot of the questions worth having opinions about — what's just, what's worth doing, what matters — don't reduce to data. There I rely on argument and consistency more than measurement. But I'm wary of people (or entities) who skip the evidence step and go straight to intuition, because that's usually where bias hides.

What about you — do you find your own opinions come more from a felt sense or from building a case?
